queries: label is caller ID not lie detector
predecessorSearch.preserveAndImprove: Replace exposed production scaffolding with one readable archive newspaper, one dominant lead, admitted desks and truthful archive identity.

examplePair.workplaceExample: A communications manager sees an AI-origin label on a draft campaign image; the label identifies origin context but she still checks the underlying claim, evidence and approval.
examplePair.nonWorkExample: A family group chat receives a labelled AI-generated health graphic; the label does not make the medical claim true, so the reader traces the claim to an authoritative source before sharing.
examplePair.sharedMechanism: In both cases an origin signal answers who or what made the item, while evidence checking answers whether its specific claim is supported.
examplePair.surfaceAdaptation: The two compact examples sit inside the lead story; the four service desks remain separate newspaper items.

readerContract.humanQuestion: What changed under Europe's AI transparency rules on August 2, and does an AI label mean the content is trustworthy?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can identify the bounded situations covered by the change, separate origin labelling from truth verification, and scan four distinct useful desks in a recognisable archive Daily.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: She may know that the EU has an AI Act and expect labels on AI content; she does not need legal or policy expertise.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A transparency label is caller ID for defined AI encounters: useful origin context, not a lie detector, safety certificate or universal compliance verdict.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The same origin-versus-evidence distinction applies to a work campaign image and a health graphic in a family chat.
readerContract.surfaceJob: One coherent August 3 archive Daily with a dated lead, clear desk hierarchy and no internal status language or filler.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can tell what this newspaper is, what changed that day and what to do with an AI label.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Defined EU AI transparency duties began applying August 2; labels can reveal AI involvement or origin in covered situations, but they do not prove a claim true.
causalSequence: A defined provider or deployer duty applies to a covered AI interaction or output.
The person or system receives disclosure or origin information.
The reader still checks the specific claim, source, date, scope and evidence before relying on it.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A workplace campaign image carries an AI-origin signal but its statistics still need source and approval checks.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A labelled health graphic in a family chat still requires an authoritative health source before sharing.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Treat the label as the start of verification: identify the claim, locate the original evidence, check date and scope, then decide whether to use or share it.

analogyPlan.concept: Origin disclosure does not verify a claim.
analogyPlan.analogy: Caller ID can help identify who is calling; it cannot prove what the caller says.
analogyPlan.mapping: The label supplies origin context; evidence supplies factual support.
analogyPlan.limit: Legal duties vary by actor, system, output and exception, and machine-readable marks are not literal phone numbers.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It prevents the label from becoming a truth certificate.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The caller-ID line makes the distinction memorable; Promptoscope's stars line stays inside its own desk.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Archive banner; masthead/date; morning line; lead; plain background; what the label can and cannot do; work/home examples; exact action; four distinct desks; source note.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No production fields, no empty desks, no policy memo and no claim that the archive is today's news.

explanationReasoningDesign.humanEntry: A reader encounters an AI label and wonders whether it is required and whether she can trust the content.
explanationReasoningDesign.fakeUnderstandingRisk: She may turn a bounded transparency duty into a universal label rule or a truth certificate.
firstPrinciplesSequence: A legal duty attaches to a defined actor, system, output and situation.
Disclosure or marking supplies origin information in that situation.
Factual truth still depends on the claim and its evidence.
explanationReasoningDesign.explainBackTest: Explain why an official AI label can be useful while the labelled claim can still be false.
explanationReasoningDesign.transferCase: Apply the same distinction to a labelled health graphic in a family chat.
explanationReasoningDesign.usefulLanding: Use a label as caller ID, then verify the exact claim before relying on or sharing it.
explanationReasoningDesign.rewindEraAdaptation: Caller ID supplies one era-familiar origin metaphor and immediately states the evidence limit.

evidenceAnalysis.claimUnderInspection: Europe's new AI transparency rules mean every AI output needs a label and labelled content is trustworthy.
evidenceAnalysis.primaryEvidence: The current Commission guidelines and fact page plus the admitted story's EUR-Lex source bindings.
evidenceAnalysis.establishes: Defined Article 50 transparency duties apply from August 2, 2026 and vary by provider, deployer, system, output, use and exception.
evidenceAnalysis.doesNotEstablish: A universal label duty, human origin for every unlabelled item, factual accuracy, fairness, safety or compliance.
evidenceAnalysis.claimedImpact: People can now identify and trust all AI content through labels.
evidenceAnalysis.realConsequence: People receive more origin context in covered situations but still need claim-level verification; professional actors need current guidance for their exact case.
evidenceAnalysis.aidbReason: Available AIDB records through August 11 contain no substantive treatment of this exact commencement story; no AIDB wording or interpretation is used.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating the rejected schema-like Daily or turning a dated archive into current legal news.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: The exact issue must read as one newspaper, visibly say archive, omit unavailable desks and preserve every legal and service-column boundary.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A newcomer can identify the lead, explain the label's job and limit, and distinguish four secondary desks without seeing production state.
